summary: Feed s065_single is degraded: IDS receives predominantly one-way traffic (105/137 TCP sessions, 76.6% unidirectional) and cannot perform stateful inspection. All other checks (duplicates, packet drops, VLANs, encrypted share, tool overload) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is delivering only one direction of each flow to the IDS port. Likely only one SPAN/mirror direction or one leg of a tap/bond is mapped to s065_single without aggregating the complementary direction. Asymmetric routing or separate ingress ports for client->server and server->client are not combined with flow affinity to the same tool port, causing 76.6% of sessions to appear unidirectional (threshold 10%).
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires both directions and full payload for TCP reassembly and signature matching. With only one side visible, it cannot reconstruct streams, correlate request/response, validate handshakes, or detect multi-packet exploits, resulting in severely degraded detection coverage and high false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow onto the same IDS tool port with flow affinity so the IDS sees complete bidirectional sessions required for stateful analysis.
